sights.w: Twin reflecting pools sit in the footprints of the fallen towers; the museum below preserves the slurry wall and artifacts.

sights.n: National Museum of the American Indian
sights.w: Free Smithsonian collection of Native art housed inside the Beaux-Arts Alexander Hamilton U.S. Custom House.
Maya Lin-designed galleries tracing 160+ years of Chinese American history on the edge of Chinatown.
Tiny Battery Park City gallery devoted to the vertical city, with mirrored floors and ceilings echoing height. Free admission.
Site where Washington took the first presidential oath and the first Congress met; a Greek Revival landmark on Wall Street.
Gothic Revival church anchoring the head of Wall Street; Alexander Hamilton is buried in its churchyard.
Manhattan's oldest church in continuous use (1766); served as a relief station after 9/11, which happened across the street.
Sacred site marking a colonial-era cemetery of free and enslaved Africans, rediscovered during 1991 construction.
The only 19th-century family home in Manhattan preserved intact inside and out, furnishings and all.
The 1913 'Cathedral of Commerce' with a jaw-dropping mosaic-and-gargoyle lobby, viewable only on booked tours.
Free 25-minute round-trip harbor ride passing the Statue of Liberty and lower Manhattan's skyline.

sights.address: Broadway at Bowling Green, New York NY 10004
sights.w: Arturo Di Modica's 7,000-pound bronze bull, an unsanctioned 1989 drop that became the icon of the Financial District.
Kristen Visbal's bronze girl now stands defiantly facing the New York Stock Exchange.
Whimsical Nolita sculpture garden saved from demolition in 2025 after a celebrity-backed community fight.
Colonial tavern where Washington bade farewell to his officers in 1783; museum upstairs, working tavern below.
Restored 1887 Eldridge Street Synagogue with a stunning stained-glass rose window by Kiki Smith.
Chinatown's largest Buddhist temple, home to a 16-foot golden Buddha, tucked beside the Manhattan Bridge.
Chinatown's social heart, where elders play xiangqi and mahjong and tai chi groups gather each morning.
A sharp-bending Chinatown lane once nicknamed the 'Bloody Angle,' now lined with murals and old shops.
Cobblestoned 17th-century lane, pedestrianized and packed with bar tables under string lights come evening.
A transplanted Irish fieldstone cottage and hillside in Battery Park City memorializing the Great Famine.
Walter De Maria's 1977 interior sculpture: a SoHo loft filled with 280,000 pounds of earth, free to visit.
Another De Maria installation: 500 polished brass rods laid in perfect rows across a SoHo gallery floor.
Santiago Calatrava's soaring white rib-cage transit hall, a winged marble concourse over the PATH station.

sights.address: Pier 55 at W 13th St, New York NY 10014
sights.w: Free floating park on tulip-shaped concrete pots over the Hudson, with lawns, overlooks and an amphitheater.

food.w: Michelin-starred ground-floor restaurant in an Art Deco tower; the golden pork katsu is the must-order.
Michelin-starred Italian-American cooking inside the landmark Puck Building, from the Major Food Group team.
Daniel Rose's Michelin-starred French room; unapologetically classic dishes in an airy candlelit space.
Chinatown's oldest dim sum parlor (1920) on a curved lane; the OG egg roll and shrimp dumplings are staples.
The Chinatown institution that put xiao long bao on the NYC map; order the crab-and-pork soup dumplings.
Michelin Bib Gourmand for made-to-order dim sum; the green snow pea leaf dumplings are the signature.
Michelin Bib Gourmand revival of the restaurant that popularized cold sesame noodles in NYC decades ago.
Late-night Cantonese standby famed for salt-baked seafood and window-hung roast duck.
Cash-only counter turning out gloriously cheap plates of char siu roast pork over rice; expect a line.
Chef Sam Yoo's diner under the Manhattan Bridge reimagining classics; the honey butter pancakes are a hit.
Basement Chinatown-American mainstay open since 1938, roast pork lo mein at all hours.
Chinatown stalwart carving crisp-skinned Peking duck tableside for wrapping in pancakes.
Billed as America's first pizzeria (1905); the coal-oven clam pie is the one to get.
The cult Nolita slice window; the curled-cup spicy spring pepperoni square draws constant lines.
Nolita red-sauce favorite; the thin-crust tie-dye pie swirls vodka sauce with pesto.
Scarr Pimentel's house-milled-flour slice shop on the LES, a wood-paneled throwback with a modern crust.
Keith McNally's bustling SoHo brasserie; steak frites and the raw bar under a zinc-and-mirror room.
The SoHo pastry lab that invented the Cronut; a rotating monthly flavor plus the DKA and cookie shot.
LES brunch institution whose fluffy blueberry pancakes with maple butter built its reputation.
Little Italy pasticceria since 1892; shell-crisp cannoli filled to order and classic sfogliatelle.
Family Italian latteria since 1925 pulling fresh mozzarella to order alongside aged cheeses and cured meats.
The oldest bialy bakery in the U.S. (1936), hand-rolling onion-centered bialys and bagels on the LES.

food.address: 137 E Houston St, New York NY 10002
food.w: Selling old-world baked potato knishes on Houston Street since 1910; a living LES relic.
No-reservations Greek taverna at the Chinatown-LES seam; flaming saganaki and grilled octopus.
Iberian-leaning seafood spot on Canal from the Hart's team; tinned fish, razor clams and vinho verde.
Unapologetically regional Indian cooking inside Essex Market; bold goat and offal-forward plates.
